extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians preparing manuscripts for publication (particularly authors submitting to the AMS Bulletin or Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing and preparing mathematical manuscripts for publication, with special rules for submissions to the American Mathematical Society's Bulletin and Transactions. Covers organization, symbol usage, typesetting constraints, manuscript preparation, figures, bibliographies, and proofreading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization of the paper into chapters, sections, paragraphs, propositions, theorems, proofs, examples, remarks, and the use of appropriate headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must settle questions such as appropriate headings and the arrangement of material; adopt a clear, self-explanatory organizational scheme so the paper's structure is evident to readers and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumeration system simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: The adoption of a system of enumeration for sections, theorems, displayed formulas, and so on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a system which is simple and self-explanatory; avoid unnecessarily complicated numbering such as II.3.6.la.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: How footnotes should be treated in the manuscript and printed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes should be assembled at the end of the paper, typed double spaced, and numbered with arabic numbers; footnote symbols (as used in Bulletin vs Transactions) should be used correctly; do not use any symbol for 'Presented to...' on the title page; a footnote symbol should not follow a mathematical symbol.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and bibliography format
rubrics_metrics.description: How works referred to in the text are to be listed and how bibliography entries are referenced in text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either 'Bibliography' or 'References' may be used. Two forms (Form I and Form II) are illustrated. Use bracketed citation marks like [1, Theorem 3.7] (Form I) or [Author 1, p. 100] (Form II). Avoid abbreviating obscure journal names; standard journals may be abbreviated per Appendix B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization and technical adjectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether to use capital or small initial letters in adjectives such as abelian, euclidean, jacobian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must be consistent throughout the paper (Rule of Uniformity); consult the journal's routine stylistic requirements where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation in technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use or non-use of hyphens in technical terms (e.g., sub-harmonic, fixed-point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a usage and maintain it consistently (Rule of Uniformity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule of Uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever usage an author adopts in a given paper should be maintained consistently throughout the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency avoids editorial queries and delays; e.g., do not alternate between 'euclidean' and 'Euclidean'—editors cannot guess the author's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mathematical symbols in running text
rubrics_metrics.description: Symbols in the text should be used so that their translation into words or phrases will require no effort of the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two explicit general rules: (1) Symbols in the text should be used in such a way that their translation into words or phrases will require no effort on the part of the reader. (2) The resulting translation should conform to the standards of good literary composition. Examples and anti-patterns given (e.g., avoid 'let e^0 be a number' or awkward symbol-first sentences unless unambiguous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual and grammatical acceptability of symbol usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid symbol usages that are visually objectionable or violate good literary composition even if they are common.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer readability and appearance; sometimes substituting words for symbols yields better appearance despite extra effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printer-available characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only such characters as the printer has in stock (see Appendix C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix C lists special types available for Bulletin and Transactions; additions are made from time to time. Using unavailable dashed/tilde/other special letters forces manual work, extra expense, and possible misalignment/errors. If special characters are required, authors should be aware of delay and cost for custom matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid putting complicated formulas into footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Many symbols are not available in footnote size; complicated formulas should not be put into footnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complicated formulas in footnotes may be unreadable or require unavailable sizes; careful organization can often eliminate the need for footnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid formulas requiring spreading in running text
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not put into the solid text any formula which would require spreading (uneven spacing) of lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such formulas are difficult for the compositor; instead display them where space permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of limits and stacked subscripts/superscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits, subscripts and superscripts in inline text must be feasible for machine setting and alignment (e.g., n directly over i; in integrals, the b directly over the a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show which inline arrangements are infeasible; when they would misalign, use displayed formulas where limits can occupy their own lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use exp() for complicated exponents in text
rubrics_metrics.description: In the text, replace e^(...) by exp(...) if the expression in the parentheses is complicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This improves readability and avoids awkward inline typesetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for binomial coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Use C_{m,n} (binomial coefficient) instead of the parenthetical form (m choose n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefers forms that set well in text and avoid awkward inline formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of membership symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended symbols for membership: use G to mean 'is a member of' (i.e., ∈), and the symbol for 'is not a member of' (i.e., ∉).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt consistent symbol usage for membership relations; ensure symbols chosen are available in printer's stock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer fractional exponents and solidus in subscripts/superscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use fractional exponents in place of radicals; a fraction occurring as subscript or superscript should be formed with a solidus (e.g., 2/3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In display, keep the number of lines occupied by a fraction as small as possible; rearrange expressions to reduce vertical size where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display long or awkwardly breaking expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Long formulas or expressions which might break awkwardly at the end of a line of text should be displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed formulas avoid awkward line breaks and improve typesetting; also allow limits/subscripts that are difficult inline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number displayed formulas only if referred to
rubrics_metrics.description: A displayed formula should be numbered only if referred to elsewhere in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbering indiscriminately prevents combining formulas or running occasional formulas into the text to facilitate galley/page breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote numbering order and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes should be numbered in the order they appear, beginning with 1 and continuing throughout the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type them double spaced at the end of the paper and follow the Bulletin/Transactions conventions for symbols where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation: typing and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should be typewritten; the text should be double spaced and displayed material should not be crowded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave plenty of space for characters to be filled in by hand; make at least one carbon copy (send carbon copy to editor, but send original—not the carbon—to printer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscripts and superscripts in manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscripts or superscripts may be filled in by hand; if typed they should be a half-space above or below the line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When handwritten, they must be carefully aligned and distinct; in doubt, mark the intended character (e.g., 'Greek chi') in the margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handwritten characters clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Handwritten characters should be made with great care and each character must be distinct in shape from every other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use margin identification like 'Greek chi', 'cap' for capitals, 'l.c.' for lower case; list of commonly-confused pairs is provided (e.g., 0/O, 1/l, z/Z, s/S, p/P).

rubrics_metrics.name: German and script letters marking
rubrics_metrics.description: German and script letters may be handwritten if accurate, but preferably type the corresponding Roman letters then underline or encircle with colored pencil to indicate the special alphabet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use colored-pencil codes (e.g., green for German, blue for script) and state meanings in margins or a separate 'instructions for the printer' sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate italics by underlining
rubrics_metrics.description: Italic type is indicated by underlining, preferably with a blue pencil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Bulletin and Transactions, theorem/corollary text is always in italics and editorial assistants will handle necessary indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omissions denoted by three raised dots
rubrics_metrics.description: Omissions should be denoted by exactly three slightly raised dots, such as ab • • • c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If commas are required, write a1, • • • , an or #1, #2, • • • , never a1 • • • an; make handwritten commas carefully so they are not mistaken for subscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish digit one and letter ell
rubrics_metrics.description: The number one is ordinarily typed as 1; the letter 'ell' should be denoted by l (dash may be written).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the solidus (/) in place of the dash may lead to typesetting errors; be explicit in notation to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and diagrams quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings and diagrams should be made with particular care since they cannot be changed or corrected in galley or page proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use black India ink on Bristol board; make drawings 2–3 times larger than final print size and allow for reduction; insert letters/symbols lightly in pencil if the drawing is for Bulletin/Transactions because they will be replaced by type letters; include only essential drawings to avoid extra expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and galley proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Galley proofs must be carefully read and corrected by the author; corrections must be clear and explicit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should request only essential changes (minor insertions/deletions are costly); replace deleted text with material occupying about the same space if possible to avoid resets; in Bulletin/Transactions, galley proofs are read in AMS office before being sent to authors—answer margin queries promptly; use standard proof-reading signs (Appendix A) consistently and place correction indications in margins with a corresponding mark in the text; margin signs should retain the order of corresponding errors and be separated by '|'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard proof-reading signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the standard set of proof-reading signs (Appendix A) when making corrections to proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard signs include delete (///), insert (A), close up (O), insert space (7F=), raise/lower, move left/right ([, ]), stet, wrong font (W.J), lower case (l.c.), use roman (rom.), italics (ital.), etc. Avoid elaborate systems of your own invention and ensure joint authors do not use non-equivalent systems in the same set of galley proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit alterations in set type
rubrics_metrics.description: Alterations in type which has been set are delicate and costly to make and should be limited to essential changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid whimsical insertions or deletions (even commas); if deleting several consecutive words, replace them with words/symbols occupying similar space to avoid tearing down and resetting lines—a costly operation that can introduce errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix C availability and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix C lists the special signs and characters available for the Bulletin and Transactions and notes costs/delays for additional characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many characters are available (Greek variants, German, script, dotted/dashed letters, superiors/inferiors). Additional characters can be made on special order but may take 4–8 weeks and cost about $4.50 per matrix (wartime conditions may vary). Authors should check Appendix C before using special symbols.
